findings.reason: the honest change is to add the follower-liveness signal to `overdue_unreconciled_runs` (or unify the two predicates) so one owner answers "which terminal pointers is nobody returning to", instead of a parallel `reckon crew forgotten` that drifts from the fence that already refuses on the same population.
findings.text: §5 builds a new `forgotten` derivation in recovery.py, but `overdue_unreconciled_runs` already returns exactly "terminal pointers past a threshold, not excused by a closure disposition" (filtering scoring/promotable/completed_unpromoted/blocked/paused over `list_live`), and the dispatch fence already consumes it at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:6724`; §5's own negative control asserts dispatch retains NO such coupling, contradicting the existing one

findings.reason: the implementing node should call `read_lane_document` and branch on its returned `unknown_fields`/`stale`/resolved fields, not re-derive the presence semantics; a forked reader is how the idle-shape rule and the router's published shape drift apart.
findings.text: the §4 headroom rule in comment c-20260923T0200 ("key on which fields are present rather than on their values"; `concurrent_requests` absent → read `concurrent_requests_instant`; document missing/older than shelf life/unreadable → dispatch nothing, record lane unreadable) is already implemented by `read_lane_document`/`read_lane_counts` (`_FIELD_KEYS` at lane_document.py:83, `blank_report` at :255, freshness/shelf-life in the returned report), yet the plan names only the `advise-the-lane-never-force-it` plan and never cites this module

findings.reason: i.e. hoist/supersede `_needs_you_runs` into the recovery.py function §2 adds and delete the cli copy, or the "live view returns the same list" parity §2 tests will be an assertion over two independent implementations that drift on the next state-vocabulary change.
findings.text: §2's needs-you list re-implements `_needs_you_runs(project, session=...)`, which already selects the owning session's runs in `FLEET_BLOCKED_STATES ∪ FLEET_UNPROMOTED_STATES` from live pointers via `_watch_snapshot`; the plan does not cite it, so a worker following §2 literally leaves two list builders over the same snapshots

findings.reason: §3 should define drain from `_fleet_counts(..., session=...).get("working", 0)==0` and its queued sibling, reusing the one partition owner, so the drain definition cannot disagree with the trailing figures the same pane renders.
findings.text: §3's drain predicate ("the owning session's working and queued runs reach zero") restates `_population_has_live_work(project, session=...)`, which already walks the owning session's live pointers and reports whether any non-terminal phase remains; the plan cites neither it nor the session-scoped `_fleet_counts(snapshots, session=...)` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:10352`), which computes the `working` count it wants

findings.reason: §2 should consume the fleet classification sets (the same ones `_fleet_counts` and `_needs_you_runs` use), not the ticker's display set plus patches, or the needs-you line and the trailing figures will classify the same run differently.
findings.text: §2 names the source of truth for its states as `NEEDS_ACTION` in `reckon/crew/ticker.py`, which is the display vocabulary; `recovery.py` already derives the classification sets (`FLEET_BLOCKED_STATES = NEEDS_ACTION - WAITING_STATES` at recovery.py:10349, `FLEET_UNPROMOTED_STATES = ("complete","completed_unpromoted","departed")` at :10341), which is why §2 must then bolt on "or is unpromoted, or needs help" to patch the missing terms

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §2 places the list composition in `reckon/crew/recovery.py` beside the fleet partition and has both the follower and the live MCP view consume it, which is the deep shape (one classifier, many readers). The depth is real provided §2 supersedes `_needs_you_runs` rather than standing beside it (see duplicate_owner).
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §5 derives a "forgotten" list in `recovery.py §5` rather than extending `overdue_unreconciled_runs`, and §4 re-derives the lane-document idle-shape rule already owned by `lane_document.py`; §2 re-derives `_needs_you_runs` and reintroduces the needs-action vocabulary from `NEEDS_ACTION` beside the fleet state sets.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan adds a needs-you list (§2), a forgotten-runs list (§5) and a lane-headroom rule (§4) without citing the existing owners that already compute each: `_needs_you_runs` (`reckon/cli.py:3215`), `overdue_unreconciled_runs` (`reckon/crew/recovery.py:9407`) and `read_lane_document` (`reckon/crew/lane_document.py:303`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §4 extends the existing `_sweep_lapsed_holds`→`sweep` path by threading the owning session rather than wrapping it, and §5's `reckon crew forgotten` is an ordinary thin CLI verb over a recovery derivation. No layer is added over machinery that cannot be extended in place.
